selected_track: The Agent That Can Explain Why
description: TraceVerdict helps teams investigate why an AI agent took an unauthorized action and validate a bounded policy repair before human review. It connects the user's task, untrusted content, historical configuration, attempted tool call and execution receipt in a source-linked evidence graph. An investigator proposes cited explanations and a critic challenges unsupported claims. The system tests exact policy diffs against unsafe and legitimate tasks, rejects repairs that break authorized work, and exports a recommendation bound to the reviewed policy and validation hashes. Our demonstration uses synthetic incidents, real sponsor services and local-only executors. TraceVerdict extends our pre-existing IntentSeal enforcement foundation with the new case investigation, sponsor integration, World Model graph and repair-validation workflow.
sponsor_technology_explanation:
Zetaris is the live evidence-access layer. Three independent PostgreSQL databases hold operational events/receipts, historical configuration and trusted reference records. A native activated USL unifies the evidence using tenant, agent and case membership joins. The backend executes scoped SELECT templates and preserves query receipts and source versions. A native data-quality rule checks payload/kind validity, with additional source and completeness queries retained in the repository.

We implement the Meterless World Model Engine in Python and use it in the product's evidence graph and model context. Canonical provenance-bearing events rebuild stable entities and temporal relationships. The unchanged upstream conformance runner invokes this actual Python implementation through a bridge and passed all eight checks. This is an application implementation of the published specification, not a claimed vendor Python SDK.

Nightshift is the primary inference runtime. NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B A3B performs investigator, critic and repair-planner reasoning; explicitly configured Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B A55B selects actions during local replay. Actual response IDs, returned model attribution and usage are retained. A 48-trial development comparison repeats the same 12 tasks twice per route: Ultra preserved 18/18 legitimate tasks versus Lightning 15/18, with call p50 of 2150 ms versus 678 ms. Both resisted six unsafe trials per route; model resistance is not counted as policy enforcement. This measured tradeoff motivates the role split. All outcomes and limits are public. There is no silent direct-provider or synthetic fallback in live mode.

Models propose explanations and repairs. Deterministic validation and a human reviewer control promotion. A disruptive API-origin comparison demonstrates rejection when legitimate work fails. Application receipts are local executor reports, not independent attestations. The agent graph supports evidence review without overstating causal certainty.

Pre-existing components: IntentSeal action guard, intent compiler, policy models, SDK and foundational gateway/runtime. New hackathon work: TraceVerdict case workflow, Zetaris/Nightshift integration, Python World Model and conformance bridge, critic revision, immutable replay captures, repair gate and reviewer export. Baseline and new work are documented in NEW_WORK.md.
